title: Clean up message boxes.
description:
Use the text and informative text fields; don't use the detailed text
field, as not all platforms have it as a concept - on macOS, it shows up
as additional text after the main text, and on Windows and X11/Wayland,
it shows up as a concealed field that can be shown with a "show the
details" button.

Clean up some dialog contents.

Get rid of the old GTK+-derived hack with the message text being split
into primary and secondary text; we now set them as separate strings.

notes.body: enabled an automatic merge when all merge checks for 89bdd1a5e03258ca1c6266c9a4d1b84f3f888e2d pass

@@ -79,24 +79,6 @@ typedef enum {
  * @param ... Printf like parameters
  * @return The newly created dialog
  */
-/*
- * XXX This is a bit clunky. We typically pass in:
- * - simple_dialog_primary_start
- * - The primary message
- * - simple_dialog_primary_end
- * - Optionally, the secondary message.
- *
- * In the Qt UI we use primary_start and _end to split the primary and
- * secondary messages. They are then added to a QMessageBox via setText and
- * setInformativeText respectively. No formatting is applied.
- *
- * Callers are responsible for wrapping the primary message and formatting
- * the message text.
- *
- * Explicitly passing in separate primary and secondary messages would let us
- * get rid of primary_start and primary_end and reduce the amount of
- * gymnastics we have to do in the Qt UI.
- */
 extern void *simple_dialog(ESD_TYPE_E type, int btn_mask,
